headline: GOLD HOLDS $4,446 AS IRAN WORSENS — HORMUZ CRISIS ADDS GEOPOLITICAL BID ATOP WEDNESDAY'S CPI TEST
snippet: Gold December futures opened at $4,446.90 on Tuesday August 11, holding above $4,400 as Iran tensions around the Strait of Hormuz continue to worsen despite ongoing Iran-Oman ceasefire talks. The geopolitical bid is adding a second layer of support on top of last week's payroll-driven rally — the Iran scenario involves a U.S. naval blockade response to continued attacks on commercial shipping, keeping a safe-haven premium baked into price. Silver at $65.39 (up 1.07% day-over-day) continued to compress the gold-silver ratio from 67x. Both catalysts now converge on Wednesday's July CPI print at 8:30 AM ET: a soft reading consistent with the July payrolls miss (−23,000 vs +180,000 consensus) would validate the dovish rate narrative and open a path toward $4,500; a hot number would test whether $4,300 holds as support, though the Iran safe-haven bid now provides an independent floor that was absent in the June–July correction.

headline: OREZONE ORE BOMBORÉ: P16 ZONE EXTENDS 600m NORTHEAST — 1.64 g/t Au OVER 46m, MRE UPDATE Q1 2027
snippet: Orezone Gold (TSX: ORE) reported August 11, 2026 drill results from its operating Bomboré Gold Mine in Burkina Faso, confirming the P16 zone extends 600 metres northeast of established P16 resources, with best intercepts including 1.64 g/t gold over 46 metres. The 2026 program totals 65,000 metres — 45,000m dedicated to resource definition — and will inform a full Mineral Resource and Mineral Reserve update expected Q1 2027. The 14km Bomboré gold system remains open at depth and along strike; Mineral Resources are historically constrained to an average depth of ~70m, making continued step-out drilling technically low-risk. Bomboré produced 97,355 ounces in H1 2026, up 34% year-on-year. At gold above $4,400, the Q1 2027 MRE update carrying ~100,000m of incremental drilling has material re-rating potential.

headline: LEGACY GOLD LEGY BANER IDAHO: LG26-004 'MOST IMPORTANT HOLE' — 2.4 g/t Au OVER 8.2m, MAIN ZONE WEST 170m
source_name: Finanznachrichten / Legacy Gold Mines Ltd. (TSX-V: LEGY)
snippet: Legacy Gold Mines (TSX-V: LEGY) reported August 11, 2026 assay results from LG26-004 — the third Phase 1 core hole at its Baner Gold Mine Property in Idaho County, Idaho — returning 1.14 g/t gold over 13.5m from surface, then 2.4 g/t gold over 8.2m including 6.6 g/t over 2.3m. VP Exploration Mike Sutton called LG26-004 'the most important hole we have drilled at Baner' as the up-plunge hole confirms the Main Zone extends 170m further west than previously defined. Phase 2 RC drilling is already underway in a ~40,000 total planned drill feet program targeting the expanded Main Zone and multiple additional areas.

headline: KINGFISHER KFR HANK PORPHYRY: 4,500m DRILLED, THREE RIGS ACTIVE — BARRICK-BACKED, GOLDEN TRIANGLE BC
snippet: Kingfisher Metals (TSX-V: KFR) provided an August 11, 2026 exploration update on its 2026 program at the HWY-37 and Forrest Kerr Projects (933 km² and 202 km²) in BC's Golden Triangle, reporting 4,500m+ drilled in seven holes across the Hank porphyry-epithermal and Cash porphyry targets with three diamond drills active. No assays have returned yet — descriptions are based on visual core observations — but Barrick Gold holds a strategic stake in the project and the 15,000m planned program is the one of the largest early-stage copper-gold porphyry programs currently drilling in BC's Golden Triangle. The Hank discovery hosts coincident soil geochemistry and IP geophysical anomalies across several kilometres, the same detection combination that identified most of BC's major copper-gold porphyry discoveries.

headline: GSP RESOURCE GSPR HIGHLAND VALLEY BC: PHASE 1 COMPLETE — 1,801m AT ALWIN GOLD AND MER COPPER, Q3 ASSAYS
source_name: Junior Mining Network / GSP Resource Corp. (TSX-V: GSPR)
snippet: GSP Resource (TSX-V: GSPR) completed its expanded 2026 Phase 1 diamond drilling program at the Alwin Mine and Mer properties in BC's Highland Valley Copper Camp on August 11, totalling 1,801 metres across 8 holes — exceeding the planned 1,200–1,500m as additional holes were added based on alteration and mineralization observed during drilling. The program followed up the 2024 Alwin discovery hole (5.04 g/t Au, 1.01% Cu over 7.9m) and also drilled the first modern test of the Mer porphyry copper target. Assays are expected in stages through Q3 2026. Alwin-Mer sits in the same Highland Valley Copper Camp geology hosting Teck Resources' 100,000 tonne/day Highland Valley Copper Mine.

headline: EXCALIBUR EXCL BELLEHELEN NEVADA: 1km SILVER-GOLD SOIL CORRIDOR EXTENDED — ZIGS AND BROKEN CABIN TARGETS DEFINED
source_name: Investing News Network / Excalibur Metals Corp. (TSX-V: EXCL)
snippet: Excalibur Metals (TSX-V: EXCL) defined multiple new silver-gold soil anomalies on August 11 at its Bellehelen Silver-Gold Project in Nye County, Nevada's Walker Lane Trend, outlining an approximately 1-kilometre corridor north of Spyglass Ridge that includes the newly identified Zigs Target and extended Broken Cabin Target. The expanded sampling connects geological vectors within a broader hydrothermal system whose historic Bellehelen district produced gold and silver since the early 1900s. A drill program is the logical next step to test the subsurface expressions of the anomaly corridor.

headline: CAMECO VS URANIUM ENERGY: WHO WINS THE NUCLEAR RESTART? — $99B SECTOR, TRUMP DOMESTIC U3O8 TAILWINDS
snippet: The Motley Fool (August 10, 2026) compared Cameco Corp. (TSX: CCO) vs. Uranium Energy Corp. (AMEX: UEC) as uranium investor picks in the nuclear revival cycle. Cameco represents ~43% of the sector's $99B combined market cap; despite a Q2 2026 earnings miss, it remains the anchor institutional uranium position with scale and balance-sheet discipline. Uranium Energy recently acquired Rio Tinto's Sweetwater mill and Wyoming assets, making it the largest U.S. uranium company by potential production capacity at 12.1 million lbs/yr — a strategically important position as Trump's domestic uranium priorities and the $80B nuclear commitment create a preference for American producers. The analysis calls UEC the better growth trade on domestic policy, Cameco the stronger long-term lower-risk hold for investors avoiding development-stage financing risk.

headline: LIT ETF +0.99% AS CHINA NEV PENETRATION HOLDS ABOVE 48% — LITHIUM 85% ABOVE YEAR-AGO, MINE RESTARTS CAP GAINS
snippet: The Global X Lithium & Battery Tech ETF (LIT) closed at $74.74, up 0.99% on August 10, as fresh July EV registration data showed China's new-energy-vehicle penetration rate holding above 48% and European deliveries suggesting a gentler post-subsidy adjustment than feared. Lithium carbonate on August 11 stood at 144,750 CNY/T — up 0.17% day-over-day but down 6% over the past month — as mine restarts (Mineral Resources' Bald Hill from May 2026 after an 18-month pause; Core Lithium's Finniss) have added near-term supply pressure. Despite month-on-month softness, lithium remains 85.58% above year-ago levels; the structural case for moving into a deficit by end-2026 as energy storage system demand accelerates remains intact per S&P Global.

headline: IF THE IRAN WAR ENDS, WHAT HAPPENS TO GOLD? — GEOPOLITICAL PREMIUM VS MONETARY FUNDAMENTALS DISSECTED
snippet: An analysis on the Canadian Mining Report examines what the resolution of the Iran conflict would mean for gold prices, separating the geopolitical safe-haven premium from the underlying monetary drivers (weak jobs data, falling September rate-hike odds, PBOC accumulation). The key finding: gold's 2025-2026 bull market is primarily driven by monetary factors — dollar debasement, central bank diversification away from Treasuries, negative real rates — which persist regardless of whether Iran and the U.S. reach a Strait of Hormuz deal. A geopolitical resolution might cause a 2-5% pullback, but would not reverse the structural bull market. For junior mining investors, this distinction matters: the companies whose share prices have been held back by geopolitical risk appetite compression (not poor fundamentals) represent the best re-rating candidates in an Iran ceasefire scenario.

headline: GDX DRAWS $2.1 BILLION IN NEW MONEY DURING JULY-AUG RALLY — VANECK: RECORD MARGINS, DISCIPLINED CAPEX
snippet: VanEck's gold equity team reports the GDX ETF absorbed $2.1 billion in net new inflows during the July-August 2026 gold rally — a significant institutional rotation into the sector. The accompanying analysis highlights that gold miners are generating record margins and free cash flow with all-in sustaining costs well below $2,000/oz at current gold prices above $4,400, and that producer conversations confirm a disciplined capital allocation posture: debt reduction and shareholder returns rather than the reckless expansion cycles that burned investors in 2011-2013. VanEck's team frames the current setup as the early innings of a gold mining bull run that has not yet been fully reflected in equity prices, with the GDX P/E in low-to-mid teens despite record sector profits — the same valuation disconnect that preceded the major 2020 and 2016 gold equity outperformance phases.
